title: Localization preserves maps from a single object to a connective complex
statement: Let C be an abelian category and D(C) its chosen localization of integer cochain complexes at quasi-isomorphisms, with localization Q. For any object M of C and complex K such that K^i is zero for i<0, the map Hom_Ch(C)(M[0],K) to Hom_D(C)(Q(M[0]),QK) induced by Q is bijective. No projectivity assumption on M is made.

source.place: Tag 05RR, derived-category localization and truncation calculus of fractions

proof.text: Surjectivity: apply Mathlib DerivedCategory.right_fac_of_isStrictlyLE_of_isStrictlyGE with a=b=0. The source of the resulting right fraction is concentrated in degree zero. Identify it with a single complex. Full faithfulness of DerivedCategory.singleFunctor and its homology comparison make the denominator an actual isomorphism; invert it before localizing.

Injectivity: apply the zeroth homology functor to equality of localized chain maps and use homologyFunctorFactors naturality. Since the incoming differential of K is zero, K.pOpcycles 0 is invertible. In the single source, homologyι 0 is invertible. Their naturality equations recover equality of the degree-zero components; from_single_hom_ext gives equality of chain maps. The delivered Lean proves both parts using Mathlib alone.
